data.why: test_officers61::test_fix_and_flank_geometry red 10/1 (flank point 54.5 deg). Probe .plan/squad7_ff_probe.gd: the doctrine picks fp at exactly 65.0 deg to the contact centroid at plan time (t232, pos 37.19,48.21); _contact keeps moving c.pos to the visible-foe centroid as front foes die (pos 38.91,48.04 at the signal, 11->5 foes) and fp is never re-aimed, so the angle to where the enemy now is drops to 54.5. chunk_abreast is irrelevant (11 men < chunk 12: ab=3 and ab=99 identical). The scenario is chaotic: with SQUAD7-3/4 assign uncross/polish all disabled it passes at dy=0 (64.3) but FAILS at a 0.25-0.5 tile start shift (59.4, 53.9; dy=1 -> assault); with current code dy=0.25/0.5 -> break (losses in the react window, odds 1.76) and the company dies. data.rule: 13.9c-12: every wall turret on a facility wall face is a post of that facility. A lost one (destroyed / wall fell) is rebought by the facility itself after wt7.rebuild_delay_s (15 s PROVISIONAL) once the face is valid and the owner can afford it: it pays (ledger cause rebuild:<def>), lays a construction site (building, built false, wt_auto true, cn_fac) on the face, emits ConstructionStarted {auto:true} + WallTurretRebuild {id, fac, cell, owner}, and posts a job on the facility job board via Sentinels7.post_job(w, fac, {id:"wt7:<site id>", kind:"build", pos: 1 tile in front of the face, prio 2.5, roles ["engineer"], slots 1, bid: site id, ttl_s 6}) refreshed every 2 s until built, done_job when built / gone. Same for AI-owned facilities. Player control first: a site the owner cancels (cancel_building) drops the post; turrets the owner places become posts.
data.ask_ENG7: a Facility Engineer that takes a job of kind "build": e.order = {"type": "build", "building_id": job.bid} (Construction.build_step does the rest; outer-face sites are reached from outside the wall, pos is the stand point), back to auto when the site is built or gone. data.finding: root cause of the save/load divergence (seq 5735): SimIndex is incremental, so a removed entity stays in SimIndex.of(w, kind) of the running world until a full rebuild, while a loaded world starts with a fresh index. Consumers must check SimIndex.alive(w, e) / w.entities.has(e.id) (the documented liveness rule). Two G7 loops do not: sim/systems/base_state7.gd _eval (both the enemy loop and the own building/unit loop: a removed own unit hit within fire_window keeps the running world under_fire) and sim/systems/sentinels7.gd threat() (~line 851). After a load both pick differently (repro .plan/db7/dbg3.gd: first diff at tick 120 = base_state7 + sent7, all entities identical).
